# Implement a store

<!-- description: The store interfaces a program implements to keep runs in a store of its own, the stores Realm ships, and the helpers a store calls. -->

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-library-reference.mjs from the API reports and the built declarations; do not edit by hand: after `npm run build`, run `npm run docs:library`. -->

A `RunStore` keeps runs; the other store interfaces keep what Realm stores beside them, such as refused answers (`FailedAttemptStore`), trace lines (`TraceBufferStore`) and registered workflows (`WorkflowRegistrar`). This page lists those interfaces, the stores Realm ships that implement them, and the helpers a store calls for its clock, its readings and its settlements.

Where the docs teach it: [Core library: the run store interface](../core-library.md#the-run-store-interface), [Testing package](../testing-package.md).

| [`clockErrorSink`](#clockerrorsink) | function | The process's waiter-error sink, or `undefined` when no host set one. |

## Functions

### applySettlement

function · public

Applies one `SettlementDelta` against `fresh`: pure, synchronous, with no I/O and no registry.
`options` carries values only.
`definition` is passed per call
(never cached) — `lease_finalizer`/`mark_finalizer` deltas do not use it (their arms never
reference the workflow definition; only `settle_step`'s terminal-edge `mintFresh` does).

#715 (b) (D-19, D6-69): `options.at` is REQUIRED — the write's ONE reading, taken by the store
after its lock. Every instant the transform mints derives from it, and an applied result's
`run.updated_at` IS `at` (the store no longer overwrites it). No clock is read here.

Amendment 1 (#715 (b)): a `seal_run` delta takes no definition (a seal must work when the workflow
is gone) and is decided here, before `definition` is touched; any other kind that arrives without a
definition is a programming-contract violation and throws a plain `Error`.

`result.run` on `applied: true` is the AS-APPLIED transform output — see
`SettlementResult`'s own doc for the never-a-re-read invariant this carries.

```ts
function applySettlement(fresh: RunRecord, delta: SettlementDelta, definition: WorkflowDefinition | undefined, options: {
    at: Date;
    cascadeGuards?: boolean;
    storeKeepsClaims?: boolean;
}): SettlementResult;
```

### assertSealIntegrity

function · public

Checks a store write against the four seal-integrity clauses and `SEAL_COHERENT`, throwing on a
violation.
Call from every store write tail that persists `next` over `stored`. Throws on violation;
returns on every honest write — including the entire pre-#367 legacy population within a
single-version fleet (the mixed-fleet caveat is a named residual, not a solved case).

```ts
function assertSealIntegrity(stored: RunRecord, next: RunRecord): void;
```

### clockErrorSink

function · public

The process's waiter-error sink, or `undefined` when no host set one.
For tests.

```ts
function clockErrorSink(): ((err: unknown) => void) | undefined;
```

### computeClaimDeadline

function · public

Computes the claim deadline for `stepName` at claim time. A CONCRETE deadline is returned ONLY
for a reliably time-boundable claim: an `execution: 'auto'` (handler-driven) step in a workflow
with NO `execution: 'finalizer'` steps (so no finalizer drain can legitimately extend the claim
past the seal). Every other claim returns `null` (→ `claim_unknown_age`): agent steps have no
reliable wall-clock bound (the dispatcher returns instantly; `timeout_seconds` is advisory), and
any step in a finalizer-bearing workflow may hold its claim through the terminal drain.

The horizon is the WORST-CASE wall-clock across every retry attempt (issue #101 follow-up —
Design Reviewer finding #4 from the A3 debate), via the shared `worstCaseScheduleSeconds`
formula above: a single-attempt bound understates a retrying step's real claim span, so a
legitimately-retrying step could be labeled `claim_stale` — and, if `idempotent`, become
eligible for a premature `realm run reclaim --all --force` re-drive — while still on an early
attempt. For `n = 1` (no `retry:`, or `max_attempts: 1`) this reduces EXACTLY to the prior
single-attempt formula `max(RECLAIM_FLOOR, perAttemptSec + MARGIN)`, so non-retry steps'
horizons are byte-unchanged.

Issue #140 AMENDMENT + correction (B2): the horizon now consumes the SAME resolved cap the
engine enforces — `(explicit total_timeout_seconds ?? worstCaseScheduleSeconds) + margin`,
via `resolveCapMs` (record §3: `(cap ?? worstCase) + margin`). This is NOT merely "the runtime
enforcement side changed; this function's formula did not" (an earlier, INCORRECT claim this
paragraph made) — the horizon's own formula changed too, and had to: a step declaring an
EXPLICIT `total_timeout_seconds` ABOVE its worst-case schedule (the legitimate long-wait
opt-in this feature exists to support) would otherwise sleep past a horizon computed from the
worst-case schedule ALONE, well before its declared cap — a premature `claim_stale` mid-
legitimate-sleep, exactly the silent-duplicate hazard this program closes. Consuming
`resolveCapMs` closes it: retry-no-cap still reduces to the worst-case schedule (unchanged,
every pre-existing pin stays byte-identical), no-retry still reduces to `perAttemptSec`
(unchanged), and retry-WITH-an-explicit-cap now widens the horizon to `cap + margin` — the
record's mandate. The prior "does not attempt to model `retry_after`" caveat remains retired
for the DEFAULT-cap population for the same reason as before (enforcement now tracks the
declared schedule there too); it is now ALSO honestly retired for the explicit-cap population,
which this correction is what actually makes true.

```ts
function computeClaimDeadline(definition: WorkflowDefinition, stepName: string, now: Date): string | null;
```

### createSystemClock

function · public

Builds a system clock with its own waiter-error sink: `now()` is `new Date()`; `at()` arms an
`unref`'d timer of at most `MAX_HOP_MS` and re-checks `now()` each time it fires.
A
waiter's synchronous throw or rejection is caught and passed to `options.onWaiterError` — never an
unhandled rejection. The sink must not throw; if it does, that throw is swallowed. Core never
writes to `console` here: the sink is the only channel. For a host or a test that wants its own
sink; the shared `systemClock` uses the process's (`setClockErrorSink`).

```ts
function createSystemClock(options: {
    onWaiterError: (err: unknown) => void;
}): Clock;
```

### decideIdempotencyPolicy

function · public

Decide what to do when an idempotency key matches an existing run, per the caller's policy.
Returns `'reuse'` (return the existing run, `created:false`) or `'supersede'` (mint a fresh run,
`created:true`); throws a `WorkflowError` for the `fail` / `reject` policies. Pure — no I/O.

Defaults (`reuse` / `use_existing`) reproduce PR 1 behavior exactly.

CONTRACT (issue #558 PR-C): this function TRUSTS the `run_phase` it is given — it is pure and
has no record to derive from beyond the `Pick<>` it receives, whose shape is public API and stays
untouched (#279 D-3 leg v). Every caller MUST pass `run_phase: deriveRunPhase(record)` (the
`PHASE_IS_GENERATED` doctrine); a caller that forwards a stale persisted label gets a decision
computed against that label — e.g. a record persisted `completed` that DERIVES `failed` yields
`reuse` under `rerun_if_failed`, silently reusing a failed run. `idempotency-policy.test.ts`'s
witness fails any in-tree call site that does not derive.

```ts
function decideIdempotencyPolicy(matched: Pick<RunRecord, 'id' | 'workflow_id' | 'run_phase' | 'terminal_state'>, options: Pick<CreateRunOptions, 'onTerminalMatch' | 'onLiveMatch'>): IdempotencyDecision;
```

### floorAtHolder

function · public

The per-key floor of a keyed create's reading, by the `created_at` of the run it supersedes or
the newest of the key's runs.
PURE: the reading was already taken, once, by
`takeReading`. When `holderCreatedAt` (the `created_at` of the run a keyed create supersedes,
or the newest among the key's runs) parses to `h`, returns `max(reading, min(h + 1 ms, reading + ε))`;
otherwise the reading. So a successor under a key is stamped strictly after the run it supersedes
whenever the clock stepped back by LESS than ε. At a backward step of exactly ε the result EQUALS
the holder's `created_at` (not `h + 1 ms`) and the canonical order is decided by the id — a known
boundary of D6-60's "up to ε". Beyond ε the cap wins and the successor may sort before its holder
(a named residual, D6-29(b)). A `created_at` that does not parse floors nothing (D6-68).

```ts
function floorAtHolder(reading: Date, holderCreatedAt?: string): Date;
```

### floorAtRecord

function · public

Floors a reading by a record's own stamp, lifting it by at most `CLOCK_SKEW_EPSILON_MS`. When the
record's `updated_at` parses (`u`), it returns `max(r, min(u, r + ε))`: monotone and capped, so a
record stamped far ahead lifts the reading by at most ε and no deadline is minted more than ε
late.
An `updated_at` that does not parse is ignored (D6-68), never `NaN`. PURE: reads no
clock. Returns a fresh `Date`.

```ts
function floorAtRecord(r: Date, record: {
    updated_at: string;
}): Date;
```

### leaseFactOf

function · public

The one reader of a claim's lease fact, on the snapshot the claim was read from. It answers:

- a claim that names no lease (no claim, or no `lease`) ⇒ `{ absent: 'unleased' }`;
- a claim whose stored `lease` is malformed (`null`, not an object, no string `id`) ⇒
  `unknown('not_a_lease')`;
- a lease the snapshot carries a fact for ⇒ that fact;
- a lease it carries none for (a store without leases holding a record saved by one with leases, a
  snapshot built without facts, a copy of one, or facts another release made) ⇒
  `unknown('not_checked')`.

`not_held` comes only from a probe.

```ts
function leaseFactOf(snapshot: Pick<Snapshot, 'lease_facts'>, claim: ClaimRecord | undefined): LeaseFact | Unleased;
```

### leaseFactsOf

function · public (beta: port): those members may change in a minor release until they settle

What the lease port `port` finds about the leases of `record`'s in-progress claims: one probe per
distinct lease id, and nothing else. A store calls it after the read or write that returned the
run, outside its write transaction and its lock.

- No port (absent or `null`) ⇒ `NO_LEASE_FACTS`, and no claim is read.
- A run whose stored `claims` is `null`, or anything but an object, has no claims; any error while
  the lease ids are collected (a record that throws when read) gives `NO_LEASE_FACTS`, so its
  claims read `not_checked`, never `not_held`.
- A claim whose stored `lease` is `null`, not an object, or has no string `id` is skipped: no probe,
  no entry (`leaseFactOf` answers `not_a_lease` for it from the claim itself).
- A probe that rejects or throws, or answers something that is not a `LeaseFact`, gives
  `unknown('io_error')` for that id. The returned promise never rejects.
- No in-progress claim names a lease ⇒ `NO_LEASE_FACTS`, with no probe.

```ts
function leaseFactsOf(port: LeasePort | null | undefined, record: RunRecord): Promise<LeaseFacts>;
```

### releaseLineOf

function · public

The release line an object carries: Realm's own classes through their release mark, a host's
class or object through `declareReleaseLine`.
`undefined` when it carries none. One property read,
inside a `try`; total.

```ts
function releaseLineOf(value: unknown): RealmBrand | undefined;
```

### setClockErrorSink

function · public

Sets the process's waiter-error sink: where the shared `systemClock`, and a test location's
clock, pass a failing waiter's error.
A host calls
it once, at its start. The sink must not throw; a throw from it is swallowed.

```ts
function setClockErrorSink(sink: (err: unknown) => void): void;
```

### takeRawReading

function · public

Takes the raw reading of `clock`: exactly one `clock.now()` call, validated, as a fresh `Date`.
A throw from `clock.now()` propagates unchanged, having spent the one reading (D6-4).
A `clock.now()` that returns an invalid `Date` fails here, loud, instead of as a `RangeError` from
`toISOString()` later. A READ takes it BEFORE it loads (D6-16): every statement about what it then
loads holds at the reading; a listing's `read_at` is this raw value.

```ts
function takeRawReading(clock: Clock): Date;
```

### takeReading

function · public

Takes a write's reading: one `clock.now()` call and no other time source, floored by `record`
when it is given (`floorAtRecord`).
When
`delta` is given (a `settleStep`), the delta's EVENT instants — the `started_at` / `completed_at`
of the evidence it carries (`eventInstantsOf`) — are folded in: `at = max(floored reading,
...events)`. Event instants are NOT capped by ε. Most are this process's own readings, taken when
the work ended; a `settle_gate` answer's `started_at` is the question's stored `opened_at`, the
reading of the program that opened it. An identity entry's `captured_at` is outside class and
never folded (D6-67). It is `foldReading` of the one raw reading.
Returns a fresh `Date`.

```ts
function takeReading(clock: Clock, record?: {
    updated_at: string;
}, delta?: SettlementDelta): Date;
```

### writtenSnapshot

function · public

The one constructor of a `Snapshot`: a record and the reading it is judged at; it reads no clock.
A store builds every snapshot it returns through it (the
reading its read or write took); the engine builds one from a write's returned `{ record, at }`.
A reply's ways speak of the record as written, never of a record read again.

#729 CW-1b: with `facts`, the `lease_facts` from `leaseFactsOf` when the store has a lease port; a
snapshot with no facts (none passed, or `NO_LEASE_FACTS`) is `{ record, at }` exactly, as before.

```ts
function writtenSnapshot(record: RunRecord, at: Date, facts?: LeaseFacts): Snapshot;
```

## Classes

### InMemoryTraceBufferStore

class · public

In-memory TraceBufferStore for use in tests and non-persistent environments.
Entries are lost on process restart (no file I/O).

Declares the fenced trio (issue #207): `append`, `read`, `delete`, and `deleteAllForRun` all
serialize on the SAME per-(runId, stepId) critical section `appendFenced`/`deleteFenced` use,
via a per-key async mutex (a promise-chain map) — every one of the operations for a given key
runs strictly after the previous operation on THAT SAME key has settled (success or failure).
Liveness posture: a hung run read hangs only that key's chain — a different key's chain is
untouched and proceeds normally (this per-key granularity is load-bearing; see the TCK's
PER_KEY_INDEPENDENCE law). The chain map's entry for a key is deleted once its own tail
settles and no newer call has chained after it, so an idle key holds no Map entry (no leak).

Issue #197 PR-1 additionally declares BOTH capability-ladder rungs (`seal` and
`writer_nonce_carriage`, `traceCapabilities`). The live-WAL internal representation is
BATCH-preserving (`Map<string, SealedWalLine[]>`, one entry per `append`/`appendFenced` call) —
NOT flattened — because `sealFenced` must be able to retire a key's exact batch history as one
unit, and each batch's own (possibly absent) writer nonce must survive independently for
carriage/budget partitioning. Every flattening surface (`read`, `readAllForRun`, `deleteFenced`'s
count, the byte-budget arithmetic) derives its answer from this representation via
`flattenWalBatches` (or direct batch arithmetic over it), reproducing the exact pre-#197
observable shape and byte formula for all-bare traffic — see `appendUnlocked`.

```ts
class InMemoryTraceBufferStore implements TraceBufferStore {
    readonly traceCapabilities: ReadonlySet<TraceCapability>;
    constructor(runReader: FenceRunReader);
    append(runId: string, stepId: string, entries: AgentTraceEntry[], options?: AppendOptions): Promise<AppendResult>;
    appendFenced(runId: string, stepId: string, entries: AgentTraceEntry[], fence: FencePredicate, options?: AppendOptions): Promise<AppendResult>;
    read(runId: string, stepId: string): Promise<BufferedEntry[]>;
    delete(runId: string, stepId: string): Promise<void>;
    deleteFenced(runId: string, stepId: string, fence: FencePredicate): Promise<number>;
    statAllForRun(runId: string, _dirEntries?: readonly string[]): Promise<{
        bytes: number;
    }>;
    deleteAllForRun(runId: string, _dirEntries?: readonly string[]): Promise<ArtifactDeletionReport>;
    deleteAllForRunFenced(runId: string, fence: RunScopedFencePredicate, _dirEntries?: readonly string[]): Promise<ArtifactDeletionReport>;
    sealFenced(runId: string, stepId: string, fence: FencePredicate): Promise<SealResult>;
    listSealedForRun(runId: string): Promise<SealedArtifact[]>;
    readAllForRun(runId: string): Promise<Record<string, unknown[]>>;
}
```

### JsonFileFailedAttemptStore

class · public

File-backed store for failed agent-attempt sidecars. Append (MCP server) + read (CLI). Best-effort:
append never throws/propagates. Lock-free: each line is ≤PIPE_BUF, so a single O_APPEND write is
atomic and interleave-safe across concurrent processes (the size bound is what buys lock-freedom —
the deliberate difference from the WAL store).

```ts
class JsonFileFailedAttemptStore implements FailedAttemptStore, OrphanSweepableStore {
    constructor(runsDir: string);
    append(runId: string, line: string): Promise<void>;
    read(runId: string): Promise<FailedAttemptReadResult>;
    deleteAllForRun(runId: string, _dirEntries?: readonly string[]): Promise<ArtifactDeletionReport>;
    statAllForRun(runId: string, _dirEntries?: readonly string[]): Promise<{
        bytes: number;
    }>;
    listOrphans(liveRunIds: ReadonlySet<string>): Promise<OrphanArtifact[]>;
}
```

## Interfaces

### AgentTraceEntry

interface · public

A single trace entry submitted by the agent. Submitted as-is; the engine
canonicalizes and assigns seq before persisting.

```ts
interface AgentTraceEntry {
    event: string;
    timestamp?: string | undefined;
    data?: Record<string, string | number | boolean | null> | undefined;
}
```

### AppendOptions

interface · public

The optional last argument of `append` and `appendFenced`: the writer's nonce.
Declaration-only: adding this parameter is NOT a separate
method-presence check in `storeDeclaresNonceCarriage` (there is no way to detect "did this
store implementation read the options bag" other than declared capability + behavior) — a
non-declaring implementation is contractually required to IGNORE it, never throw or otherwise
error on receiving one; the tool layer (PR-2) is responsible for never passing a nonce to a
non-declaring store.

```ts
interface AppendOptions {
    writerNonce?: string;
}
```

### AppendResult

interface · public

What a trace buffer reports after an append: how many entries and bytes this writer holds against
its limits, and the whole file's when the store keeps them (`TraceBufferStore.append`).

```ts
interface AppendResult {
    buffer_count: number;
    buffer_bytes: number;
    limit_count: number;
    limit_bytes: number;
    final_limit_entries: number;
    final_limit_bytes: number;
    file_count?: number;
    file_limit_count?: number;
    file_bytes?: number;
    file_limit_bytes?: number;
}
```

### ArtifactDeletionReport

interface · public

What a store reports about the artifacts it just deleted: the bytes it deleted.

Bytes are a STORE-DEFINED, internally-consistent measure — exact on-disk bytes for the
filesystem stores, a documented approximation elsewhere (a Postgres store uses the same
`SUM(octet_length(...))` expression on both its stat and its delete). The only guarantee ACROSS
the two methods is the L6 identity below. Cross-store sums are meaningful where the wired stores
share a measure, which the CLI's filesystem stores do.

```ts
interface ArtifactDeletionReport {
    bytes_deleted: number;
}
```

### BufferedEntry

interface · public

An `AgentTraceEntry` with the engine's ordering timestamp in milliseconds, and the writer nonce
that carried it, if any. The nonce is re-attached from the line the entry was originally appended
in.
NEVER fabricated for a genuinely bare line.

```ts
interface BufferedEntry extends AgentTraceEntry {
    _internalTs: number;
    _nonce?: string;
}
```

interface · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

A rotation: the new key's text, how long the old key stays as the previous (1–604,800 seconds),

### CallbackKeyStore

interface · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

The signing keys of a callback store (`CallbackStore.keys`): for each (workflow, host), a current
key and, for a while after a rotation, a previous one.
`workflowId` and `host` are each 1–255 characters, compared byte for byte; a key's text is 64
lowercase hex characters. Every method but `delete` takes ONE raw reading of the store's clock,
refused or applied; `delete` takes none; a malformed request throws before any reading, and its
message never repeats a candidate key. A previous counts only while it is live: past its
`expires_at` it is absent for every method, and no method returns it. Refusals are results, never
thrown. Keys are kept apart from the callback rows and the runs: a run's purge leaves them.

```ts
interface CallbackKeyStore {
    read(workflowId: string, host: string): Promise<CallbackKeyPair>;
    make(workflowId: string, host: string, candidate: string): Promise<CallbackKeyMakeResult>;
    rotate(workflowId: string, host: string, request: CallbackKeyRotateRequest): Promise<CallbackKeyRotateResult>;
    endPrevious(workflowId: string, host: string): Promise<CallbackKeyEndResult>;
    replace(workflowId: string, host: string, candidate: string): Promise<CallbackKeyReplaceResult>;
    delete(workflowId: string, host: string): Promise<CallbackKeyDeleteResult>;
    list(): Promise<readonly CallbackKeyListing[]>;
}
```

interface · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

Where a run's caller asked to be told the run finished (`CreateRunOptions.callback`).
`url` is the address as given (1–2,048 characters), `host` the label the caller computed from it
(1–255) and `webhook_id` a uuid the caller made, the same on every try.

```ts

    readonly url: string;
    readonly host: string;
    readonly webhook_id: string;
}
```

interface · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

One callback row as a store keeps it, for store implementers only.
It carries the address, the frozen body and the claim token, so it is never rendered: the port's

field is omitted, never `null`.

```ts
interface CallbackRow {
    readonly run_id: string;

    readonly host: string;
    readonly webhook_id: string;
```

### CallbackStore

interface · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

A store's callback store (`RunStore.callbacks`): one row per run, written by `create`.
`due`, `claim` and a `retry` mark each take ONE raw reading of the store's clock, refused or
applied; `read`, `countPending`, `freezeBody`, the other marks and the purge pair take none; a
malformed request throws before any reading. A run without a row is no error.

```ts
interface CallbackStore extends PerRunArtifactStore {
    read(runId: string): Promise<CallbackView | undefined>;
    countPending(): Promise<number>;
    due(limit: number): Promise<CallbackItem[]>;
    claim(runId: string, request: CallbackClaimRequest): Promise<CallbackClaimResult>;
    freezeBody(runId: string, token: string, body: string): Promise<CallbackFreezeResult>;
    mark(runId: string, token: string, result: CallbackMarkRequest): Promise<CallbackMarkResult>;
    readonly keys: CallbackKeyStore;
}
```

### Clock

interface · public

The clock a run store reads the time from: `now()` and `at()`.

`now()` returns the current instant as a FRESH `Date` on every call: mutating a returned `Date`
changes nothing else.

`at(when, fn)` runs `fn` once when the clock reaches `when` and returns a cancel; after the cancel
`fn` never runs. A `when` already past runs at the next opportunity (on a system clock the next
tick; on a test clock the next `advance`). Its scope (D6-8, D6-45): it serves waits for an instant
STORED on a record or derived from stored fields alone (an expiry; reminder occurrence
k = `opened_at + k·R`), and (#964; #597 D3a) the instant a question's escalation or single fallback
reminder falls due: a duration added to when the question was posted (its Slack time, clamped between
`opened_at` and the store's reading the reminders started from). It never drives the
default ceiling (`gate_unanswered` is a fact derived at read, with no writer and no timer) and never
replaces a poll or any other duration timer: those stay on real timers.

```ts
interface Clock {
    now(): Date;
    at(when: Date, fn: () => void | Promise<void>): () => void;
}
```

interface · public

Where `realm listen` remembers the webhook events it has seen, so an event delivered twice starts

### ExpireGateDelta

interface · public

Carries out a gate's frozen timeout disposition once the gate has expired unanswered.
Fenced by
`gateId` ONLY — same fencing shape as `SettleGateDelta` (a gate's authority is
bearer-gateId-credentialed) — so a stale/duplicate expire attempt for a gate that has since
been superseded (resolved by a human, or already expired by a racing enactment point) NOOPs or
refuses rather than silently expiring the WRONG (newer) gate. Carries no caller-supplied
`evidence`, unlike every other delta kind: the disposition (and therefore the evidence shape)
is decided INSIDE `applyExpireGate` itself by reading the frozen `PendingGate` fields — the
`applyAbortEdge` cancel-gate precedent (settlement.ts) for a transform building its own
evidence via `captureEvidence` rather than a caller-supplied array.

```ts
interface ExpireGateDelta {
    kind: 'expire_gate';
    gateId: string;
}
```

interface · public

A store of failed agent-attempt records, kept per run. The core owns the interface, so a store in

never throws; `read` returns the run's records in append order (the engine's ranking reads that

### Listing

interface · public

What `JsonFileStore.listWithDiagnostics` returns beside its diagnostics: every record with the
reading it is judged at, and the listing's own reading. It is the shape `list` returned until
#616 c4.

- `read_at` is the RAW reading, taken ONCE before the first record was read (D6-16).
- each snapshot's `at` is `read_at` floored by that record's own `updated_at` (`floorAtRecord`):
  every statement about a record holds at its own `at`.
- `consistent_snapshot` says whether the records were read as ONE cut: `true` for a store that reads
  them in one synchronous pass (the in-memory store), `false` for one that reads them one by one
  (the JSON-file store reads each file in turn, so two rows may come from different moments).

```ts
interface Listing {
    snapshots: Snapshot[];
    read_at: Date;
    consistent_snapshot: boolean;
}
```

not an array, unlike `SettleStepDelta.evidence`.


### OpenGateDelta

interface · public

Opens a human gate on a claimed step.
#715 (b) (D-20, D6-12): the delta carries
DURATIONS, never instants — `pendingGate` is the gate without `opened_at`/`expires_at`, and
`timeoutSeconds` its declared timeout; the transform writes `opened_at = at` and, when
`timeoutSeconds` is given, `expires_at = at + timeoutSeconds`. Everything else in `pendingGate` is
carried verbatim. This is the OPENING kind only: a restore (none exists) carries the full
`PendingGate` with its frozen instants in its own delta kind. `claimToken` is compared the same
absent≡absent way `SettleStepDelta.claimToken` is.

```ts
interface OpenGateDelta {
    kind: 'open_gate';
    step: string;
    claimToken?: string;
    pendingGate: OpeningGate;
    timeoutSeconds?: number;
    evidence: EvidenceSnapshot[];
}
```

### OrphanArtifact

interface · public

One candidate orphan artifact — an absolute path this store owns, plus enough metadata for the
caller to apply its own age floor.

```ts
interface OrphanArtifact {
    path: string;
    runId: string;
    mtimeMs: number;
}
```

### OrphanSweepableStore

interface · public

A store whose files for a run can outlive the run's own file, and that lists those left behind;
it deletes nothing (`listOrphans`).

```ts
interface OrphanSweepableStore {
    listOrphans(liveRunIds: ReadonlySet<string>): Promise<OrphanArtifact[]>;
}
```

### OutboundEntry

interface · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

One row of a run's outbound ledger as a store keeps it, for store implementers only. It carries
the lease token, the holder's proof, so it is never rendered and never returned by the port:
every entry the port returns is an `OutboundEntryView`.
An unset field is omitted, never `null`.

```ts
interface OutboundEntry {
    readonly entry_key: string;
    readonly type: 'reminder' | 'escalation';
    readonly occurrence?: number;
    readonly of_max?: number;
    readonly status: 'pending' | 'sent' | 'failed';
    readonly lease_token: string;
    readonly lease_deadline: string;
    readonly attempts: number;
    readonly last_at?: string;
    readonly last_outcome?: string;
    readonly sent_at?: string;
    readonly created_at: string;
}
```

### OutboundLeaseRequest

interface · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

A lease of one reminder or of the escalation of a run's open question. `leaseToken` is the caller's
own (1–200 characters); `leaseSeconds` a positive finite number, cut to `OUTBOUND_LEASE_MAX`;
`occurrence` a positive whole number.

```ts
interface OutboundLeaseRequest {
    readonly what: {
        readonly type: 'reminder';
        readonly gateId: string;
        readonly occurrence: number;
    } | {
        readonly type: 'escalation';
        readonly gateId: string;
    };
    readonly leaseToken: string;
    readonly leaseSeconds: number;
}
```

### OutboundLedger

interface · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

A store's outbound ledger (`RunStore.outbound`). `lease` and `mark` each take exactly ONE raw reading
of the store's clock, refused or applied, and a malformed request throws before it; `read`,
`statAllForRun` and `deleteAllForRun` take none. A run that does not exist is no error: `lease`
answers `gate_not_open`, `read` answers no rows, and the purge pair reports zero.

```ts
interface OutboundLedger extends PerRunArtifactStore {
    lease(runId: string, request: OutboundLeaseRequest): Promise<OutboundResult>;
    mark(runId: string, request: OutboundMarkRequest): Promise<OutboundResult>;
    read(runId: string): Promise<OutboundEntryView[]>;
}
```

### OutboundMarkRequest

interface · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

The mark of a leased reminder or escalation: `sent` with the outcome `ok`, or `failed` with
`refused:<code>`, the code 1–64 characters of `a`–`z`, `0`–`9` and `_`.

```ts
interface OutboundMarkRequest {
    readonly what: OutboundLeaseRequest['what'];
    readonly leaseToken: string;
    readonly result: 'sent' | 'failed';
    readonly outcome: 'ok' | `refused:${string}`;
}
```

### PerRunArtifactStore

interface · public

A store that keeps files of its own for each run and deletes them all for a run when asked, as
`realm run purge` does.

```ts
interface PerRunArtifactStore {
    deleteAllForRun(runId: string, dirEntries?: readonly string[], options?: {
        expectVersion?: number;
    }): Promise<ArtifactDeletionReport>;
    statAllForRun(runId: string, dirEntries?: readonly string[]): Promise<{
        bytes: number;
    }>;
}
```

### PurgedItem

interface · public

A deleted run's tombstone, as a scan with `include_purged` gives it. It holds the run's id, its
workflow, when it was purged, its seal's arm, and the phase and derivation stamp it had when
purged (its record is gone, so its phase cannot be derived again).

```ts
interface PurgedItem {
    kind: 'purged';
    run_id: string;
    workflow_id: string | null;
    purged_at: string;
    sealed_by_arm: string | null;
    run_phase: RunPhase;
    phase_version: string;
}
```

### RealmBrand

interface · public

What one copy of one package says about itself, on the prototype of each class it defines.

```ts
interface RealmBrand {
    readonly package: string;
    readonly generation: string;
    readonly version: string;
    readonly url: string | null;
}
```

interface · public

Summary returned by `JsonFileStore.reconcileKeys`.

```ts
}
```

### RegistryListing

interface · public

What a registrar's diagnostic listing returns (`WorkflowRegistrar.listWithDiagnostics`).

```ts
interface RegistryListing {
    workflows: WorkflowDefinition[];
    unreadable: UnreadableRegistryEntry[];
    mismatched: Array<{
        file: string;
        id: string;
    }>;
}
```

### ReleaseStepDelta

interface · public

Releases a step's claim without settling the step. It is the shared shape behind both the
capability-block release and the compensating un-claim.
NEVER terminal, writes NO `settled` entry — the step returns to eligible.

```ts
interface ReleaseStepDelta {
    kind: 'release_step';
    step: string;
    claimToken?: string;
    capabilityBlock?: {
        requirement: {
            kind: 'handler' | 'adapter';
            name: string;
        };
        code: string;
    };
    evidence?: EvidenceSnapshot[];
}
```

### ReplayRecord

interface · public

A persisted replay snapshot: the result of replayRun() + the metadata that produced it.

```ts
interface ReplayRecord {
    id: string;
    origin_run_id: string;
    workflow_id: string;
    overrides: string[];
    results: ReplayStepResult[];
    created_at: string;
}
```

### ReplayStepResult

interface · public

One step of a replay: whether its preconditions held in the run, and with the overrides.

```ts
interface ReplayStepResult {
    step_id: string;
    preconditions_original: boolean;
    preconditions_replay: boolean;
    changed: boolean;
    has_preconditions: boolean;
}
```

### ReplayStore

interface · public

Where replays of a run are kept: each saved with its overrides and results, and read back by id.

```ts
interface ReplayStore {
    save(record: Omit<ReplayRecord, 'id' | 'created_at'>): Promise<ReplayRecord>;
    get(replayId: string): Promise<ReplayRecord>;
}
```

### RunListing

interface · public

What `JsonFileStore.listWithDiagnostics` returns: the same `Listing` `list` returns, beside the
diagnostics. The `Listing` is `snapshots`, `read_at` and `consistent_snapshot`.

```ts
interface RunListing extends Listing {
    unreadable: UnreadableRunFileEntry[];
    copies: UnreadableRunFileEntry[];
}
```

### RunRow

interface · public

One run as a scan's `'row'` projection gives it: the record's own fields, with four derived or
renamed. `run_phase` is the derived phase, `terminal_state` is the column's 0/1 as a boolean,
`run_version` is the record's `version` and `pending_gate` is the gate's id or `null`.
No params, no
evidence.

```ts
interface RunRow {
    id: string;
    workflow_id: string;
    run_phase: RunPhase;
    terminal_state: boolean;
    sealed_by_arm: string | null;
    created_at: string;
    updated_at: string;
    idempotency_key: string | null;
    rerun_of: string | null;
    run_version: number;
    pending_gate: string | null;
    completed_steps: string[];
    in_progress_steps: string[];
    failed_steps: string[];
}
```

### RunStore

interface · public (beta: callbacks, claimStep.hold, leases, outbound): those members may change in a minor release until they settle

Where a program keeps its runs: it creates, reads, updates, lists, claims and settles them,
reading the time from its own clock.

```ts
interface RunStore {
    readonly clock: Clock;
    persistsClaims: boolean;
    readonly purgesRuns: boolean;
    readonly leases?: LeasePort | null;
    readonly outbound?: OutboundLedger | null;
    readonly callbacks?: CallbackStore | null;
    readonly persistedRunRecordFields?: ReadonlySet<LoadBearingRunRecordField>;
    create(options: CreateRunOptions): Promise<CreateResult>;
    get(runId: string): Promise<Snapshot>;
    update(record: RunRecord): Promise<Snapshot>;
    scan(filter: ScanFilter, options: ScanOptions & {
        projection: 'row';
    }): AsyncGenerator<ScanPage<'row'>, void, undefined>;
    scan(filter: ScanFilter, options: ScanOptions & {
        projection?: 'record';
    }): AsyncGenerator<ScanPage<'record'>, void, undefined>;
    scan(filter: ScanFilter, options: ScanOptions): AsyncGenerator<ScanPage<'record'> | ScanPage<'row'>, void, undefined>;
    scanListed?(filter: ScanFilter, options: Omit<ScanOptions, 'projection'>): AsyncGenerator<ListedScanPage, void, undefined>;
    resolveKey(workflowId: string, key: string): Promise<KeyAnswer>;
    tombstonesSince(): Promise<string>;
    claimStep(runId: string, stepName: string, definition: WorkflowDefinition, claimant?: Attributed, hold?: LeaseHold): Promise<Snapshot>;
    settleStep(runId: string, delta: SealRunDelta): Promise<StoreSettlement>;
    settleStep(runId: string, delta: Exclude<SettlementDelta, SealRunDelta>, definition: WorkflowDefinition): Promise<StoreSettlement>;
    stampSeal?(runId: string, sealedBy: SealedBy, expectedVersion: number): Promise<StampSealResult>;
}
```

### ScanFilter

interface · public

The filters of a store's scan.
Every filter given must hold. `key` needs `workflow`: a
key is a key of one workflow. `created_since` and `updated_since` are stamps in the store's one
shape (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`), compared as text and inclusive.

```ts
interface ScanFilter {
    workflow?: string;
    phase?: RunPhase;
    terminal?: boolean;
    key?: string;
    created_since?: string;
    updated_since?: string;
    include_purged?: boolean;
}
```

### ScanOptions

interface · public

How a scan pages: its page size, its projection, and the id it starts after. `pageSize` is
required, a whole number from 1 to `SCAN_MAX_PAGE_SIZE`; `projection` is `'record'` (the default:
each run as `get()` returns it) or `'row'` (each run as a `RunRow`); `after` starts the scan
after that id (the last id of the page before, the `--after` cursor).

```ts
interface ScanOptions {
    pageSize: number;
    projection?: 'record' | 'row';
    after?: string;
}
```

### ScanPage

interface · public

One page of a store's scan: its items in id order, its one reading, and the cursor for the next
page. `read_at` is the page's one reading; `consistent_snapshot` says the page was read in one
read transaction (one per page under WAL); `derived_at_read` counts the rows whose phase was
stamped by another derivation (each was derived at read; 0 when none); `next_after`, when the
page is full, is the cursor the next page starts after (the page's last id).

```ts
interface ScanPage<P extends 'record' | 'row'> {
    items: ScanItem<P>[];
    read_at: Date;
    consistent_snapshot: true;
    derived_at_read: number;
    next_after?: string;
}
```

### SealedArtifact

interface · public

One sealed artifact for a single run and step.
A key may accumulate several sealed artifacts (repeated reclaim/settle-time seals),
 distinguished by ascending `seq`.

```ts
interface SealedArtifact {
    step_id: string;
    seq: number;
    lines: SealedWalLine[];
}
```

### SealedWalLine

interface · public

One line of a WAL as read back, live or sealed.
Defined in CORE, not
mcp-server (where the fs store's own file-local `WalLine` type lives), because
`listSealedForRun`'s return type must be usable without any core-adjacent caller importing an
mcp-server-local type. The fs store's `WalLine` gains the identical optional `nonce` field and
stays structurally assignable to this type (never a separate, divergent shape).

```ts
interface SealedWalLine {
    ts: number;
    entries: AgentTraceEntry[];
    nonce?: string;
}
```

### SealRunDelta

interface · public

Seals a run at the run level: an abandon, a cleanup, a webhook spawn failure or an extension load
failure.
The transform seals through `sealRunLevel` with
the write's one reading as every seal-tier instant (`abandoned_at`).

- `expected_version` is the version the writer judged the run at: a stored record whose version
  differs is REFUSED `moved` (the transform returns it; the store THROWS it as
  `STATE_SNAPSHOT_MISMATCH`, exactly as `update()` does — D6-65).
- a record already terminal returns `already_terminal` with the fresh record.
- `release_claims` clears `claims` AND `in_progress_steps` in the same write (D6-66).
- `identity_entry` is appended to `extension_identity` verbatim — its `captured_at` is outside
  class, minted before any store, and never folded into the reading (D6-67).

```ts
interface SealRunDelta {
    kind: 'seal_run';
    arm: SealArm;
    reason: string;
    expected_version: number;
    release_claims: boolean;
    identity_entry?: ExtensionIdentityEntry;
}
```

### SettleGateDelta

interface · public

Resolves an open gate with a person's choice.
Fenced by `gateId` ONLY — zero claim arms (§3's own note: "fence = gateId
ONLY (L20)"), since a gate's authority is bearer-gateId-credentialed (D-5: RECORDED, not
enforced — `respondedBy` below is an evidence passthrough, read by no arm).

```ts
interface SettleGateDelta {
    kind: 'settle_gate';
    gateId: string;
    choice: string;
    respondedBy?: string;
    claimToken?: string;
    sender?: {
        user: string;
        forms: readonly string[];
    };
    projectAnswerers?: readonly string[];
    evidence: EvidenceSnapshot[];
}
```

### SettleGuardDelta

interface · public

Records a guard step's evaluated outcome.
Guards are never claimed (`eligibility.ts:418` — `findEligibleGuardSteps`
has no claim concept), so this delta carries no `claimToken` at all — fence = ⊥. `evidence` is
SINGULAR (the `MarkFinalizerDelta` precedent — one guard evaluation, one evidence snapshot),
unlike `SettleStepDelta.evidence`'s array.

`resolutionError` is REQUIRED when `outcome === 'resolution_error'`; `abort` is REQUIRED when
`outcome === 'abort'` — a violation of either throws a plain contract-violation `Error` in the
transform (the `settlement.ts:228-234` precedent), never a `WorkflowError` (a caller-programming
error, not a predicate outcome).

```ts
interface SettleGuardDelta {
    kind: 'settle_guard';
    step: string;
    outcome: 'pass' | 'resolution_error' | 'abort';
    evidence: EvidenceSnapshot;
    resolutionError?: {
        condition: string;
        unresolvable_path: string;
        cause?: string;
    };
    abort?: {
        conditions: Array<{
            condition: string;
            resolved_value: unknown;
            passed: boolean;
        }>;
        abort_message?: string;
    };
    evaluatedAtVersion?: number;
}
```

### SettleStepDelta

interface · public

A step settlement intent — the caller reports what a claimed step's dispatcher/handler produced;
`applySettlement` (settlement.ts, the pure transform) decides whether it applies against fresh
state. `claimToken` is compared against `fresh.claims[step].token` via absent≡absent
`tokensEqual` (record §2) — omit it only for a caller that genuinely has no fencing token yet
(pre-token-adoption; #197's grandfathered-claims precedent).

`abort` is REQUIRED in practice when `outcome === 'abort'` (handler-abort only — see the design
record §1's OUT list: guard aborts stay on the legacy CAS path through increment 2+, so this
delta shape never needs to carry `conditions`, unlike `RunRecord.aborted_at`'s guard-abort
variant). `applySettlement` throws a plain contract-violation `Error` (never a `WorkflowError` —
this is a caller-programming-error path, not a runtime predicate outcome) if `outcome==='abort'`
and `abort` is missing; every real caller always supplies both together.

```ts
interface SettleStepDelta {
    kind: 'settle_step';
    step: string;
    outcome: SettleStepOutcome;
    claimToken?: string;
    evidence: EvidenceSnapshot[];
    failureMessage?: string;
    abort?: {
        stepId: string;
        abortMessage: string;
    };
}
```

### Snapshot

interface · public

One record and the reading it is judged at.
Built only by this module.

```ts
interface Snapshot {
    readonly record: RunRecord;
    readonly at: Date;
    readonly lease_facts?: LeaseFacts;
}
```

### TraceBufferStore

interface · public

Where an agent step's trace entries wait, per run and step, while the agent works; the engine
reads them when it records the step's result.

```ts
interface TraceBufferStore {
    readonly traceCapabilities?: ReadonlySet<TraceCapability>;
    append(runId: string, stepId: string, entries: AgentTraceEntry[], options?: AppendOptions): Promise<AppendResult>;
    read(runId: string, stepId: string): Promise<BufferedEntry[]>;
    delete(runId: string, stepId: string): Promise<void>;
    deleteAllForRun(runId: string, dirEntries?: readonly string[]): Promise<ArtifactDeletionReport>;
    statAllForRun(runId: string, dirEntries?: readonly string[]): Promise<{
        bytes: number;
    }>;
    readAllForRun(runId: string): Promise<Record<string, unknown[]>>;
    appendFenced?(runId: string, stepId: string, entries: AgentTraceEntry[], fence: FencePredicate, options?: AppendOptions): Promise<AppendResult>;
    deleteFenced?(runId: string, stepId: string, fence: FencePredicate): Promise<number>;
    deleteAllForRunFenced?(runId: string, fence: RunScopedFencePredicate, dirEntries?: readonly string[]): Promise<ArtifactDeletionReport>;
    sealFenced?(runId: string, stepId: string, fence: FencePredicate): Promise<SealResult>;
    listSealedForRun?(runId: string): Promise<SealedArtifact[]>;
}
```

### UnreadableFileEntry

interface · public

A registered copy a registry of files could not read, named by its file.

```ts
interface UnreadableFileEntry {
    file: string;
    workflow_id?: never;
    class: FileUnreadableClass;
    errno?: string;
    reason: string;
    repair?: string;
}
```

### UnreadableIdEntry

interface · public

A registered copy a registry with no files (the SQLite registry) could not read, named by its
workflow's id.
Never carries `file` or `errno`: no file holds it, and no class on this
 arm is an OS error.

```ts
interface UnreadableIdEntry {
    workflow_id: string;
    file?: never;
    errno?: never;
    class: IdUnreadableClass;
    reason: string;
    repair?: string;
}
```

### UnreadableRunFileEntry

interface · public

One run file the JSON store could not read as a run, as a listing reports it
(`RunListing.unreadable`).
`reason` is the fault sentence and `repair` the way out (`realm run list` prints both); `facts`
are the damaged file's facts (no content), which a decision over every run names when it fails
closed.

```ts
interface UnreadableRunFileEntry {
    file: string;
    path: string;
    class: StoredFileClass;
    errno?: string;
    reason: string;
    repair: string;
    facts: UnreadableFileFacts;
}
```

### ValidationErrorSummaryEntry

interface · public

A single whitelisted Ajv error — value echoes (`params`/`data`) are intentionally excluded.

```ts
interface ValidationErrorSummaryEntry {
    instancePath: string;
    schemaPath: string;
    keyword: string;
    message: string;
    additional_property?: string;
    missing_property?: string;
}
```

### WorkflowRegistrar

interface · public

Where a program registers its workflows and reads them back by id.

```ts

    register(definition: WorkflowDefinition): Promise<void>;
    get(workflowId: string): Promise<WorkflowDefinition>;
    list(): Promise<WorkflowDefinition[]>;
    listWithDiagnostics?(): Promise<RegistryListing>;

}
```

## Types

### CallbackClaimedItem

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

A claimed row: the item with the instants a sender judges its ends from.

```ts
type CallbackClaimedItem = CallbackItem & Pick<CallbackRow, 'last_status'> & {
    readonly finished_at: string;
    readonly first_attempt_at: string;
};
```

### CallbackClaimResult

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

What a claim answers: the claimed item and the claim's one reading, or why it did not apply.

```ts
type CallbackClaimResult = {
    readonly applied: true;
    readonly item: CallbackClaimedItem;
    readonly at: string;
} | {
    readonly applied: false;
    readonly reason: 'no_row' | 'not_pending' | 'stale' | 'run_not_finished';
};
```

### CallbackFreezeResult

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

What freezing the body answers.

```ts
type CallbackFreezeResult = {
    readonly applied: true;
} | {
    readonly applied: false;
    readonly reason: 'no_row' | 'not_pending' | 'lost_claim' | 'body_set';
};
```

### CallbackItem

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

A row ready to send, as `due` returns it: for the sender only, never rendered.

```ts
type CallbackItem = Pick<CallbackRow, 'run_id' | 'workflow_id' | 'host' | 'webhook_id' | 'attempts' | 'next_attempt_at' | 'body'> & {
    readonly url: string;
};
```

### CallbackKeyEndResult

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

What `endPrevious` answers: whether a live previous was there to remove.

```ts
type CallbackKeyEndResult = {
    readonly ended: true;
} | {
    readonly ended: false;
    readonly reason: 'no_previous';
};
```

### CallbackKeyReplaceResult

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

What `replace` answers: the new current key, or why it wrote nothing.

```ts
type CallbackKeyReplaceResult = {
    readonly applied: true;
    readonly key: CallbackKeySlot;
} | {
    readonly applied: false;
    readonly reason: 'no_current' | 'readable';
};
```

### CallbackKeyRotateResult

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

What `rotate` answers: the pair it wrote, or why it wrote nothing.

```ts
type CallbackKeyRotateResult = {
    readonly applied: true;
    readonly current: CallbackKeySlot;
    readonly previous: CallbackKeySlot;
} | {
    readonly applied: false;
    readonly reason: 'no_current' | 'current_unreadable' | 'previous_live';
};
```

### CallbackKeySlot

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

One slot of a pair, as the store holds it.
`readable` carries the key's text (64 lowercase hex characters) and `key_fp`, its fingerprint;
`unreadable` is a slot the store holds but cannot read (sealed under another master key), with the
fingerprint of the master key that sealed it. `created_at` and `expires_at` are the store's own
readings; `expires_at` is set on a `previous` only.

```ts
type CallbackKeySlot = {
    readonly slot: CallbackKeySlotName;
    readonly state: 'readable';
    readonly key: string;
    readonly key_fp: string;
    readonly created_at: string;
    readonly expires_at?: string;
} | {
    readonly slot: CallbackKeySlotName;
    readonly state: 'unreadable';
    readonly master_fp: string;
    readonly created_at: string;
    readonly expires_at?: string;
};
```

### CallbackKeySlotInfo

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

One slot as `list` gives it: what `read` answers, without the key's text. `readable` carries the
key's fingerprint, `unreadable` the fingerprint of the master key that sealed it.

```ts
type CallbackKeySlotInfo = {
    readonly slot: CallbackKeySlotName;
    readonly state: 'readable';
    readonly key_fp: string;
    readonly created_at: string;
    readonly expires_at?: string;
} | {
    readonly slot: CallbackKeySlotName;
    readonly state: 'unreadable';
    readonly master_fp: string;
    readonly created_at: string;
    readonly expires_at?: string;
};
```

### CallbackKeySlotName

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

The name of a slot: `current` signs; `previous` is the key a rotation replaced, kept for a while.

```ts
type CallbackKeySlotName = (typeof CALLBACK_KEY_SLOTS)[number];
```

### CallbackLastStatus

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

The last answer a try got: an HTTP status (100–599), or a word for a try that got none.

```ts
type CallbackLastStatus = number | (typeof CALLBACK_LAST_STATUS_WORDS)[number];
```

### CallbackMarkRequest

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

A try's outcome: delivered (a 2xx status), another try after a wait in seconds, or failed.

```ts
type CallbackMarkRequest = {
    readonly kind: 'delivered';
    readonly lastStatus: number;
} | {
    readonly kind: 'retry';
    readonly afterSeconds: number;
    readonly lastStatus: CallbackLastStatus;
} | {
    readonly kind: 'failed';
    readonly lastStatus: CallbackLastStatus;
};
```

### CallbackMarkResult

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

What a mark answers.

```ts
type CallbackMarkResult = {
    readonly applied: true;
} | {
    readonly applied: false;
    readonly reason: 'no_row' | 'not_pending' | 'lost_claim';
};
```

### CallbackStatus

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

The state of a callback row: `pending` while it may be tried, then `delivered` or `failed`.

```ts
type CallbackStatus = (typeof CALLBACK_STATUSES)[number];
```

### CallbackView

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

A callback row as the port's `read` returns it: no address, body, token or webhook id.

```ts
type CallbackView = Omit<CallbackRow, 'run_id' | 'webhook_id' | 'url' | 'body' | 'claim_token'>;
```

type · public

What `WorkflowRegistrar.getCapped` resolves to.

```ts
type CappedRead = {
    definition: WorkflowDefinition;
} | {
    over: {
        bytes: number;
    };
};
```

### CreateResult

type · public

What a run store's `create` returns: the record with the reading the create used, and whether it
was written.
A keyed create that returns an existing run (`created: false`)
has spent its reading too, and returns it.

```ts
type CreateResult = Snapshot & {
    created: boolean;

```

### FencePredicate

type · public

The four facts a fenced trace-buffer operation can be conditioned on.
Derived
from every fenced call site on `60a21eb` — one member per former guard; the fifth, `gc`'s
`run_absent`, left with that command (#616 PR-2c).

A member is a condition on the fenced method's OWN target and never names a target of its own:
the run is always the method's `runId`, and the two step members (`step_open_for_trace`,
`step_not_in_progress`) are evaluated against the method's `stepId`. A fence therefore cannot
condition one step while the write lands on another, and only the per-step methods accept a step
member (`StepScopedFencePredicate`); the run-wide `deleteAllForRunFenced` takes a
`RunScopedFencePredicate`. The per-step methods accept every member: a run-scoped member
conditions the run the step belongs to. A member carries only its own fields:
`assertFencePredicate` refuses any other own, enumerable, string-keyed property — every field
an object literal or parsed JSON can carry.

- `step_open_for_trace` — `append_trace`'s write-time re-check (`appendFenced`): the run exists,
  is not terminal, and the method's step is in none of `completed_steps`/`failed_steps`/
  `skipped_steps`/`in_progress_steps`. `run_version` is the version the CALLER observed on its
  own pre-lock read:
  it is the `run_version` the `run_not_found` refusal reports (there is no run to read a version
  from once the run is gone) — the former guard closed over the same value.
- `run_absent_or_terminal` — `realm run purge`'s trace-buffer fence (`deleteAllForRunFenced`): the
  run no longer exists, or its DERIVED phase is terminal.
- `run_at_version` — reclaim's version fence (`deleteFenced`, `sealFenced`): the run's `version`
  equals the one reclaim decided on. The run must EXIST: an absent run is refused with the run
  store's own `STATE_RUN_NOT_FOUND` (see `FENCE_REQUIRES_RUN`).
- `step_not_in_progress` — the settle-time seal fence (`sealFenced`): the method's step has left
  `in_progress_steps`. The run must EXIST (same as `run_at_version`).

```ts
type FencePredicate = {
    kind: 'step_open_for_trace';
    run_version: number;
} | {
    kind: 'run_absent_or_terminal';
} | {
    kind: 'run_at_version';
    version: number;
} | {
    kind: 'step_not_in_progress';
};
```

### FencePredicateKind

type · public

The names of the conditions a fenced trace-buffer write checks before it writes
(`FencePredicate.kind`).

```ts
type FencePredicateKind = FencePredicate['kind'];
```

### FenceRunReader

type · public

The read a fence is evaluated against: the lock-free `RunStore.get`. It is the read the former
guards used, safe against an atomic rename.

```ts
type FenceRunReader = Pick<RunStore, 'get'>;
```

### FileUnreadableClass

type · public

The classes a registry of files (the JSON registry) gives a registered copy it cannot read: eight
in all. What the probe finds before any byte is read (`missing`: the file went between the
directory read and the probe; `unreadable`: an OS error reading it; `not_a_file`: a directory
where the file belongs; `empty`; `registry_broken`: the registry directory itself) and what the
read finds (`parse`: not JSON, or JSON that fails the checker; `newer`: a later version of Realm
registered it; `legacy`: an older one did).

```ts
type FileUnreadableClass = ProbeFailureClass | 'parse' | 'newer' | 'legacy';
```

### IdempotencyDecision

type · public

The action a store should take for a matched run.

```ts
type IdempotencyDecision = 'reuse' | 'supersede';
```

### IdUnreadableClass

type · public

The classes a registry with no files (the SQLite registry) gives a registered copy it cannot
read: `legacy`, `newer` and `parse`. `legacy`: an older version of Realm registered it; `newer`:
a later one did; `parse`: a copy that is not JSON or fails the checker, or a damaged pointer row
(no copy under the pointer, or one that is not JSON text), whose entry has no `repair` because
its reason names the remedy.

```ts
type IdUnreadableClass = 'legacy' | 'newer' | 'parse';
```

### KeyAnswer

type · public

Who holds an idempotency key, read in one snapshot: the run that holds it, the deleted runs that
carried it, or no run. `held` names the run that holds it; `purged` lists the deleted runs that
carried it, when no run does; `unseen` says no run carries it and no kept tombstone records one.
`since` is the tombstone horizon: a run purged at or
before it may have left no tombstone.

```ts
type KeyAnswer = {
    state: 'held';
    run_id: string;
} | {
    state: 'purged';
    runs: Array<{
        run_id: string;
        purged_at: string;
    }>;
    since: string;
} | {
    state: 'unseen';
    since: string;
};
```

### LeaseFact

type · public

What a probe found. `unknown` always carries its reason; the other three never do.

```ts
type LeaseFact = {
    readonly state: 'held' | 'not_held' | 'absent';
    readonly basis: 'kernel_lock';
} | {
    readonly state: 'unknown';
    readonly basis: 'kernel_lock';
    readonly reason: LeaseProbeReason;
};
```

### LeaseFacts

type · public

The facts about the leases of a run's in-progress claims, by lease id. Frozen, with no prototype,
and read only with `Object.hasOwn` (through `leaseFactOf`), so an inherited name such as
`constructor` is never a fact. Made only by `leaseFactsOf` and `NO_LEASE_FACTS`.

The brand is a key no object has (`never`), so a plain object is not a `LeaseFacts` without a cast;
it is a string key, not a `unique symbol`, so the type is the same in the built package as in its
source (a store type-checked against one and used against the other). What makes the rule hold at
run time is the reader: it reads only objects that carry the release mark of a copy of this release
(`LeaseFactsClass`).

```ts
type LeaseFacts = {
    readonly [leaseId: string]: LeaseFact;
} & {
    readonly '#LeaseFacts': never;
};
```

```ts
type LeaseHoldResult = {
```

type · public

Why a probe could not say whether a claim lease is held (`LeaseFact`'s `unknown` state).

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

Why a store could not make a claim lease, from the error the operating system or SQLite gave

### ListedRecord

type · public

A run as a listing of runs gives it: the record, with each evidence entry's `model_text` left
out and the evidence read-only. So `update` refuses it, and a listing's record is never written
back over the texts it left out. Every record fits into it.

```ts
type ListedRecord = Omit<RunRecord, 'evidence'> & {
    readonly evidence: readonly Omit<EvidenceSnapshot, 'model_text'>[];
};
```

### ListedScanItem

type · public

One item of a listing of runs (`RunStore.scanListed`): a run as a `ListedSnapshot`, or
a tombstone. Every `'record'` scan item fits into it.

```ts

    kind: 'run';
```

### LoadBearingRunRecordField

type · public

The `RunRecord` fields the engine relies on enough that a store must declare which of them it
round-trips (`RunStore.persistedRunRecordFields`).
This is a CLOSED set — a field qualifies via EITHER
(a) a real, verified READ-SITE consumer whose absence corrupts control flow (see
`RunStore.persistedRunRecordFields`'s own doc for the consumer list) — the first four below —
OR (b) a WRITE-SITE disclosure-integrity advisory, whose non-durability is surfaced LOUDLY
(a runtime warning) rather than silently dropped — `defaulted_steps` (issue #220 PR-2), which
has no read-site consumer in-repo today (reading it is PR-3's `$settlement` namespace) but whose
silent loss on a non-declaring store would misrepresent a run's true defaultedness to any
external consumer inspecting the persisted record directly. Not an open-ended "everything
RunRecord might ever carry":
 - `capability_blocks` — read by `findCapabilityBlockedSteps` (capability.ts), which returns
   `[]` on `undefined`; a store that drops it makes a genuinely-blocked step silently look
   unblocked to `get_run_state` / `list` / `run-agent`.
 - `workflow_context_snapshots` — read by the execution loop's `=== undefined` branch, which
   re-snapshots when absent; a store that drops it loses snapshot HISTORY (current context
   self-heals via re-snapshot, but prior snapshots are gone).
 - `extension_identity` — read by the execution loop's drift-evidence append (issue #119) and
   `realm run inspect --check-drift`; a store that drops it resets the drift baseline every
   execution, so drift can never accumulate or be detected.
 - `validation_rejections` — read by `countRejection`'s exhaustion-threshold gate (issue #220,
   execution-loop.ts) on every counted rejection; a store that drops it resets the count to
   zero every write, so a persistently-invalid agent step never reaches the threshold and the
   exhaustion terminalization this field exists for silently never fires (the wedge #220 kills
   quietly resurrects on such a store).
 - `defaulted_steps` — a run-level convenience aggregate of steps that settled via their
   declared `validation_exhaustion.default_output` (issue #220 PR-2). No read-site consumer
   in-repo (PR-3's `$settlement` namespace reads per-step evidence instead); a store that drops
   it loses only the run-level convenience marker — the per-step evidence truth is unaffected —
   but the engine surfaces that loss as an explicit envelope warning rather than staying silent.
 - `settled` / `finalizer_ledger` (issue #279, increment 1) — read by `applySettlement`'s own
   predicate (`entryOf`/`leaseFinalizerArms`/`markFinalizerArms`) on every `settleStep` call; a
   store that drops either one makes its OWN next settle/lease/mark blind to prior settlement
   history, corrupting the idempotence/fencing guarantees `settleStep` exists to provide.
   DECLARATION-COHERENCE (TCK-asserted): a store that declares `settleStep` MUST declare BOTH
   of these fields — declaring the operation without the fields it depends on is a dishonest
   declaration, not merely an incomplete one. Dormant in this PR: nothing writes either field
   until PR-B migrates the seal sites, so a store declaring them today gains a dormant gate,
   never a behavior change. Joining this CLOSED set (rather than an open one) is deliberate:
   bumping it forces every full-set-declaring store's own fidelity TCK to grow two new cases at
   the SAME compile, so a store cannot silently drift out of sync with what settleStep needs.

```ts
type LoadBearingRunRecordField = 'capability_blocks' | 'workflow_context_snapshots' | 'extension_identity' | 'validation_rejections' | 'defaulted_steps' | 'settled' | 'finalizer_ledger' | 'sealed_by';
```

### MarkFinalizerResult

type · public

The result a `mark_finalizer` delta reports for one finalizer's handler: `completed` or `failed`.
They are the two live outcomes of `finalizer_ledger[name].status`; `pending` and `voided` are
never a mark delta's own result: they are prior or other-path states the predicate reads, and
this delta never writes them.

```ts
type MarkFinalizerResult = 'completed' | 'failed';
```

type · public

The gate an `open_gate` delta opens, without its instants: everything a `PendingGate` holds but
`opened_at` and `expires_at`. The transform mints those two from the write's one reading `at`, so
no gate is ever born expired.

```ts
type OpeningGate = Omit<PendingGate, 'opened_at' | 'expires_at'>;
```

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

type · public

Realm's
homes carry this type, so a command that needs a member never meets a registrar without it.

```ts
type RealmWorkflowRegistrar = WorkflowRegistrar & Required<Pick<WorkflowRegistrar, 'listWithDiagnostics' | 'getCapped'>>;
```

### RunScopedFencePredicate

type · public

The members that condition only the run — the only ones the run-wide `deleteAllForRunFenced`
accepts. The per-step methods accept them too: a run-scoped member conditions the run the step
belongs to.

```ts
type RunScopedFencePredicate = Exclude<FencePredicate, StepScopedFencePredicate>;
```

### ScanItem

type · public

One item of a scan's page: a run in the scan's projection, or a tombstone.

```ts
type ScanItem<P extends 'record' | 'row'> = {
    kind: 'run';
    run: P extends 'record' ? Snapshot : RunRow;
} | PurgedItem;
```

### SealResult

type · public

The outcome of `sealFenced`; `TraceBufferStore.sealFenced` holds the full contract.

```ts
type SealResult = {
    sealed: true;
} | {
    sealed: false;
    reason: 'absent' | 'capped';
};
```

### SettlementDelta

type · public

The delta kinds `RunStore.settleStep` accepts.
A concrete discriminated
union — no structural intersections, no duck-typing.

**Union-openness contract (issue #279, increment 2, PR-C — design record §2, angles fold 1):**
this union is OPEN — kinds may be added in future minors (e.g. the increment-3 per-gate-timeout
candidate on the design record's residuals list). A RE-IMPLEMENTING store (a multi-statement
backend, e.g. a future Postgres store's `settleStepForTenant`) MUST refuse-loud (throw a
contract-violation error) on an unrecognized `kind` — NEVER default-arm it. Silently applying an
unrecognized kind's fields under a generic/default case is actively dangerous: `SettleGateDelta`
has no `step` field at all, so a default-arm implementation reading `delta.step` would silently
mis-write (write `undefined` as a step name) rather than crash where the bug is introduced.

```ts
type SettlementDelta = SettleStepDelta | LeaseFinalizerDelta | MarkFinalizerDelta | OpenGateDelta | SettleGateDelta | SettleGuardDelta | ReleaseStepDelta | ExpireGateDelta | SealRunDelta;
```

### SettlementRefusalReason

type · public

Every refusal or no-op reason `settleStep` can return as `SettlementResult.reason`.
`drain_pending` is left out: it is the purge guard's own thrown `STATE_RUN_BUSY` reason, never a
`settleStep` return value, so a `settleStep` implementation must never construct it.

```ts
type SettlementRefusalReason = 'already_settled' | 'already_leased' | 'already_marked' | 'already_released' | 'already_open' | 'already_settled_by_other' | 'settled_outcome_divergence' | 'run_terminal' | 'claim_lost' | 'gate_mismatch' | 'run_not_terminal' | 'ledger_not_pending' | 'lease_held' | 'lease_lost' | 'rank_blocked' | 'not_eligible' | 'gate_choice_conflict' | 'choice_not_eligible' | 'gate_open_wait' | 'answerer_mismatch' | 'not_expired' | 'no_disposition' | 'moved' | 'already_terminal';
```

### SettlementResult

type · public

The result of applying one `SettlementDelta` against fresh state.

`run` on `applied: true` is the AS-APPLIED TRANSFORM OUTPUT — pre-serialization, pre-fidelity-
filtering — and must NEVER be a re-read of what the store persisted. This is the #220 disclosure
invariant's own precedent (execution-loop.ts:2723-2729: the complete-seal envelope reads
`defaulted_steps`/`settled_by_default` off the STAMPED PRE-PERSIST record, never the round-
tripped one) generalized to every settlement result: a lossy store's round-trip would otherwise
silently break disclosure exactly where it matters. Every `settleStep` implementation MUST
return the transform's own output object here, not a subsequent `get()`/re-read.

`run` on `applied: false` is FRESH STATE — the very state the predicate refused/no-opped
against — with NO write performed (version unchanged).

```ts
type SettlementResult = {
    applied: true;
    run: import('./run-record.js').RunRecord;
    transitioned: boolean;
    pendingFinalizers: readonly string[];
    guards?: ReadonlyArray<{
        step: string;
        outcome: 'pass' | 'abort' | 'resolution_error';
    }>;
    gateClaim?: GateClaimVerdict & {
        claim?: {
            holder?: Attributed;
            since?: string;
        };
    };
    lateAnswer?: {
        gateId: string;
        choice: string;
        gateClaim: GateClaimVerdict & {
            claim?: {
                holder?: Attributed;
                since?: string;
            };
        };
        expiresAt: string;
    };
} | {
    applied: false;
    reason: SettlementRefusalReason;
    run: import('./run-record.js').RunRecord;
    gate?: PendingGate;
    winningChoice?: string;
    choices?: string[];
    allowed?: string[];
    sender?: string;
    persisted?: string;
    gateClaim?: GateClaimVerdict & {
        claim?: {
            holder?: Attributed;
            since?: string;
        };
    };
    expected?: number;
    stored?: number;
};
```

### SettleStepOutcome

type · public

The outcomes a `settle_step` delta's caller can report for the step being settled: `complete`,
`fail` or `abort`. They mirror the three places the engine seals a step: complete, fail, and a
handler's abort.

```ts
type SettleStepOutcome = 'complete' | 'fail' | 'abort';
```

type · public

The outcome of a `RunStore.stampSeal` attempt.
Both refusal reasons
are PREDICATE outcomes, returned rather than thrown, and both carry the record as it stands so
the caller can report on it without a second read.

```ts
type StampSealResult = {
    stamped: true;
    run: RunRecord;
} | {
    stamped: false;
    reason: 'already_stamped' | 'not_terminal';
    run: RunRecord;
};
```

### StepScopedFencePredicate

type · public

The members that condition one step — evaluated against the fenced method's own `stepId`.
Only the per-step methods (`appendFenced`, `deleteFenced`, `sealFenced`) accept them.

```ts
type StepScopedFencePredicate = Extract<FencePredicate, {
    kind: StepScopedKind;
}>;
```

### StepScopedKind

type · public

The fence conditions that are about one step; only the per-step fenced methods accept them.

```ts
type StepScopedKind = {
    [K in FencePredicateKind]: (typeof FENCE_TARGETS_STEP)[K] extends true ? K : never;
}[FencePredicateKind];
```

### StoreSettlement

type · public

What a run store's `settleStep` returns: the transform's result plus the write's one reading
`at`. It is returned on an applied write and on a predicate refusal (both took the reading, after
the lock).
A throw before the lock (a missing run) spends none.

#729 CW-1b: `lease_facts`, as on a `Snapshot`: what the store's lease port found about the
leases of `run`'s in-progress claims after the write (applied or refused). Present only when a
claim names a lease and the store has a lease port.

```ts
type StoreSettlement = SettlementResult & {
    at: Date;
    lease_facts?: LeaseFacts;
};
```

### TraceCapability

type · public

The optional rungs a trace buffer store can declare, `seal` and `writer_nonce_carriage`
(`TraceBufferStore.traceCapabilities`).
Implication runs **upward-requires-downward ONLY**: `writer_nonce_carriage` requires
`seal`; `seal` requires the fenced trio (issue #207). **The fenced trio ALONE stays fully
legal** — a store declaring neither rung is still a fully conforming implementation (the
shipped realm-cloud Postgres state; non-seal trio stores keep the #207 destructive-drain
posture forever, not a transitional gap). `TraceBufferStore.traceCapabilities` below is the
declaration; `storeDeclaresSeal`/`storeDeclaresNonceCarriage`/`validateTraceCapabilities`
(this file) are the ONLY authoritative way to check a rung — no ad-hoc `typeof` checks for
these two rungs anywhere else in the codebase (TCK, tools, or engine).

```ts
type TraceCapability = 'seal' | 'writer_nonce_carriage';
```

### Unleased

type · public

What `leaseFactOf` answers for a claim that names no lease.

```ts
type Unleased = {
    readonly absent: 'unleased';
};
```

type · public

A registered copy a listing could not read (`RegistryListing.unreadable`).
Each entry carries exactly one of


### CLOCK_READ_CLASSES

const · public

The five classes of a clock read: what a run store's clock governs (`write`, `read`, `event`) and
what it does not (`outside`, `duration`).
The clock census test
classes every read in the source by them, and the docs table of what the clock governs is generated
from them (`docs/reference/core-library.md`).

```ts
const CLOCK_READ_CLASSES: {
    readonly write: "An instant a write records on the run (`updated_at`, a claim's deadline, an opened question's `opened_at`): the store's reading, taken once inside the write.";
    readonly read: "The instant every statement about a record a read returns is judged at (`as_of`): the store's reading, taken before the load.";
    readonly event: "An instant the engine records with what happened (a step's start and end, a drive failure, a guard's evidence): the store's clock, read where it happens.";
    readonly outside: "An instant compared with no instant the store's clock gave (a log line, a signature window, `Retry-After`, a price day, a request's start compared with another's): the host's clock, each read named in the census with its reason.";
    readonly duration: "A duration (elapsed time, a budget, a timeout): the monotonic clock, never compared with an instant.";
};
```

### FENCE_TARGETS_STEP

const · public

Whether a member conditions one step — evaluated against the fenced method's own `stepId`.
Keyed by every kind, so a new member cannot be added without deciding it; the two types below
and `isStepScopedFence` are derived from it.

```ts
const FENCE_TARGETS_STEP: {
    readonly step_open_for_trace: true;
    readonly run_absent_or_terminal: false;
    readonly run_at_version: false;
    readonly step_not_in_progress: true;
};
```

### LEASE_PROBE_REASONS

const · public

Why a probe could not say whether a lease is held: a closed list. `not_checked` is for a caller that
did not probe at all (from CW-1b); the store's probe answers the other four.

```ts
const LEASE_PROBE_REASONS: readonly [
    "not_checked",
    "cannot_open",
    "not_a_lease",
    "permission",
    "io_error"
];
```

### LEASE_UNAVAILABLE_REASONS

const · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

Why a store could not make a lease: a closed list, from the error the operating system or SQLite gave.

```ts
const LEASE_UNAVAILABLE_REASONS: readonly [
    "permission",
    "no_space",
    "too_many_files",
    "io_error"
];
```

### systemClock

const · public

The shared system clock a store uses when nothing else is said (a `JsonFileStore` on an ordinary
directory, an `InMemoryStore` built without a clock). `now()` is `new Date()`; `at()` works as
`createSystemClock`'s does (D6-7), and a waiter's failure goes to the process's sink, read
when the waiter fails (`setClockErrorSink`); with no sink set it is re-thrown from a
microtask — loud, never swallowed (03 §A.1, D-22).

```ts
const systemClock: Clock;
```

- [`WAY_VERBS`](run-and-drive-a-run.md#way_verbs): Every verb a way can name, as a closed list (`WayVerb`).
- [`WayOn`](run-and-drive-a-run.md#wayon): One act a party can take on a run, told apart by its `verb`.
- [`WayVerb`](run-and-drive-a-run.md#wayverb): The acts a way names: answer a question, run a step, have the engine carry out what it owes, read the run, end it, register its workflow again, or send a question's form to the person (`Base.verb`).
- [`WebhookAuth`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#webhookauth): How a webhook trigger checks that a request is genuine: a shared secret, GitHub's or Stripe's signature, an HMAC, or none (`WebhookTrigger.auth`).
- [`WebhookTrigger`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#webhooktrigger): A workflow's webhook trigger: the path it answers, how it checks requests, which requests it takes, how it drops repeats, and how it maps a payload to run params.
- [`WorkflowContextEntry`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#workflowcontextentry): A single named entry in the workflow_context section.
- [`WorkflowContextSnapshot`](read-a-runs-record.md#workflowcontextsnapshot): Snapshot of a single workflow context entry taken at run start.
- [`WorkflowCopyFault`](write-a-handler.md#workflowcopyfault): What a registered copy that is a JSON object lacks to be a workflow: a numeric `schema_version`, an `id`, `steps`, or the legacy shape.
- [`WorkflowDefinition`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#workflowdefinition): A workflow as the loaders return it: its id, name and version, its params schema, its steps, and its services, protocol and trigger when it has them.
- [`WorkflowError`](write-a-handler.md#workflowerror): The error Realm throws and records, carrying a code, a category and what the agent does next.
- [`WorkflowErrorOptions`](write-a-handler.md#workflowerroroptions): What a `WorkflowError` is built with: its code and category, what the agent does next, whether it may be tried again, and the optional facts, step and ways on.
